Polish: all 5 criteria binary (scored/polish/judge.toml lines 19-61). Although the dimension is named polish, every row is an observable invariant with a crisp threshold, not a degree of craft: hro_pol_live_board (note text unchanged, still document.activeElement, scroll offset within 2 px), hro_pol_live_thread (draft/focus kept, view at newest), hro_pol_earlier_place (anchor message same position within a few pixels), hro_pol_failed_send (visible explanation, text kept, sent once), hro_pol_session_resume (sign-in prompt, per-user drafts). No graded quality spectrum is collapsed into binary; the template's own polish rows are binary too. Visual: all 5 craft criteria (hro_vis_type, hro_vis_color, hro_vis_layout, hro_vis_hierarchy, hro_vis_consistency) are type="likert", points=5, weight 1, each with a described anchor at every level 5,4,3,2,1 (scored/visual/judge.toml lines 19-92, e.g. hro_vis_type lines 19-32: '5: clear consistent type scale, readable names, labels and messages, deliberate hierarchy ... 1: typography broadly illegible or unstructured.'). No anchor level is missing.
